name: W/Z bialgebra
summary: A W-spider merge followed by a Z-spider copy equals Z-copies followed by W merges.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg. Read from right to left (the dot on the right), it merges its legs: $|0\cdots0\rangle\mapsto|0\rangle$, a single excitation maps to $|1\rangle$, and everything else to $0$.

The phase-free Z-spider and the W-spider satisfy a bialgebra law: merging two wires with a W-spider and then copying with a Z-spider is the same as copying each input with a Z-spider and merging the copies pairwise with W-spiders. This is axiom 6a of Hadzihasanovic's ZW-calculus, there written with the black monoid and the 'mixed' white comonoid, and generalises to any number of inputs and outputs ($\mathrm{ba}^{n,m}$; in the thesis, with a label $r$ on the Z-spider, $ba_{zw}$).

Unlike the [W bialgebra](../w-bialgebra/), the crossing wires here are an ordinary swap: they can never both carry $|1\rangle$ in a non-zero term.
parameter_notes: n inputs and m outputs (shown for n = m = 2); holds for any numbers of inputs and outputs.
